subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (NexaCare)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@nexacare.com>
Cc: Elliot Green <elliot.green@nexacare.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (NexaCare)

Hi Sofia / Elliot —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Good discussion — below is a short recap + proposed next steps so we can keep momentum for the bake-off. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- High inference cost at peak volume (billing surprises across endpoints).
- Latency spikes for 99th percentile requests impacting agent workflows.
- Need for stronger controls around PHI handling and auditability for clinical data.

Primary goals for the pilot/bake-off:
1) Demonstrate 10–20% lower unit cost at 95% latency target vs current provider.
2) Maintain <300ms median and <700ms p99 for the 1–2k qps scenario.
3) Show audit/logging + KMS integration to satisfy compliance evidence.

Decision criteria (what NexaCare will score vendors on):
- Cost per effective token (incl. batching/caching benefits)
- P99 latency under load
- Security posture (KMS, audit logs, SOC2 evidence)
- Integration effort + time-to-production
- Support / escalations SLA

Proposed bake-off plan (attached: Redwood-bakeoff-plan.pdf, sample-eval-prompts.csv):
- Test window: Jun 22–26 — we provision a trial cluster and run your 3 representative workloads.
- Tests: latency/cost under steady-state and spike loads, PHI-handling validation, end-to-end integration smoke tests.
- Deliverables: test runbook, raw logs, consolidated scoring matrix, and a short exec summary.

Open questions for you:
- Can you confirm the proxy/egress constraints for the trial environment (VPC peering or SSH tunneling)?
- Who should we invite on the engineering kickoff (names + emails)?
- Any procurement gating items we should prep for (PO process, pre-signed contracts)?

Next steps / asks:
- Sofia: confirm test window and provide point of contact for infra (name + contact).
- NexaCare procurement: share any standard SOW/PO timelines so we can align.
- From Redwood: we’ll send a detailed runbook and schedule the kickoff call next week.

Attaching: Redwood-bakeoff-plan.pdf (test plan), sample-eval-prompts.csv

Thanks — excited to run this for you.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192
From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@nexacare.com>

Cc: Elliot Green <elliot.green@nexacare.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (NexaCare)

Thanks Aditya — this looks great and captures the conversation. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Priorities: cost and PHI controls are our top two. If a vendor can demonstrably lower unit cost without sacrificing p99, they move to the top of our list.
2) Procurement: we typically need a PO within 30 days of agreeing on terms; I’ll loop in procurement once we finalize the trial scope.
3) Kickoff: include our infra lead (Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@nexacare.com>) and compliance (Tanya Li <tanya.li@nexacare.com>).

Open items for Redwood: 
- Can you confirm whether the trial will run in our VPC (preferred) or on Redwood-managed infra? If in our VPC, what access/ports do you need?
- Please include a short note in the runbook about how you handle encrypted-at-rest keys and audit log retention periods.

Also — can you show a short comparison matrix vs VendorX (they’re currently in scope) highlighting where Redwood saves on tokens/cost? If you can include a rough estimate in the runbook, that’d be helpful for our internal scoring.

Thanks again — we’re aligned to run Jun 22–26 pending infra confirmation.

Sofia Ramirez
Director, ML Platforms
NexaCare
sofia.ramirez@nexacare.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 18:00:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (NexaCare)

Internal — forwarding Sofia’s reply and the NexaCare asks. High level: they prefer the trial in their VPC and need Miguel + Tanya on the kickoff. Procurement timeline is ~30 days.

Action items: 
- Rishi: can you own the bake-off test harness (latency/cost runs) and produce a short vendor comparison vs VendorX? Aim to include token-level cost estimates.
- Dev: can you prep a short security note about KMS/on-prem key options and retention/audit log caps so we can include in the runbook?
- Marissa / Lauren: I’ll need help with the pricing/discount scenario and an outline of the SLA we can offer for the trial.

Please reply with availability for a 30-minute internal sync tomorrow morning — I want us aligned before we send the runbook to NexaCare.

Thanks,
Aditya
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (NexaCare)

I’ll take ownership of the test harness and vendor comparison. Quick notes: 
- I’ll prepare a short smoke suite that runs their 3 representative prompts across the following configurations: Redwood-prod-standard (quantized), Redwood-batched (aggressive batching), and VendorX-baseline.
- Metrics: median/p99 latency, tokens-per-inference cost estimate (we’ll include estimated infra cost + token math), and model output quality (basic BLEU/ROUGE-style scoring on their sample prompts).
- I’ll attach bakeoff-test-plan.md and a preliminary comparison by EOD Mon (Jun 14).

One ask for infra: if the trial runs in NexaCare VPC we’ll need a temporary IAM role + a small NAT egress rule to allow our runners to pull images and push logs. I’ll spell this out in the runbook.

Rishi

Redwood Inference
